_about: Source registry for the IASC Humanitarian Reset & Coordination Intelligence Assistant (demo mode). Hand-built from the content actually published on /sol/reset/ and /sol/reset/overview/ on 23 November 2026, plus the richer indicator set already maintained in /sol/reset/v3/data/indicators.json. Nothing here is invented: every citation points at a document, URL or on-page table that exists in this repository or at the linked URL. Edit this file, not assistant.js, when a figure or source changes.

evidence_tiers.1: Official IASC / endorsed sources and official institutional material (the Stocktake report and presentation, the IASC Secretariat's own site).
evidence_tiers.2: Authoritative official UN, humanitarian-organization or standard-setting sources (OCHA, UNDP, EU statements on behalf of IASC donors).
evidence_tiers.4: General knowledge, inference or hypothetical content — includes anything this assistant synthesizes itself, and the whole Simulate mode.

glossary.def: Inter-Agency Standing Committee — the primary mechanism for inter-agency humanitarian coordination, established June 1992 following UN General Assembly Resolution 46/182.
The IASC's current reform and stocktake effort, organized around four pillars: Define, Deliver, Devolve, Defend.
Pillar of the Reset concerned with prioritizing needs — e.g. concentrating response where severity is highest, and simplifying planning cycles.
Pillar of the Reset concerned with operational reform and reach — e.g. cluster simplification, pooled funding, people reached.
Pillar of the Reset concerned with localization — shifting resources, decisions and participation toward local and national actors.
Pillar of the Reset concerned with standing by humanitarian principles and frontline colleagues under pressure. Treated qualitatively; no quantitative indicators are reported on the page.
Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan — a country-level plan; 20 existed in the 2026 cycle per the Stocktake.
Humanitarian Programme Cycle — the planning cycle whose median completion time the Stocktake tracks (171 days in 2026, against a 160-day end-2027 target).
Country-Based Pooled Fund — OCHA-managed pooled funding mechanism; $4.53bn in contributions as of 2 October 2026 per the Stocktake.
Global Humanitarian Overview — the annual appeal document; GHO 2026 targeted 148M people and required $35.07bn.
The two highest bands on the Joint Intersectoral Analysis Framework severity scale, used to identify the most severe humanitarian needs.
Emergency Directors Group — part of the IASC structure, per the Secretariat's structure page.
Operational Policy and Advocacy Group — part of the IASC structure, per the Secretariat's structure page.
Emergency Relief Coordinator — chairs the IASC, per the Secretariat's membership and structure pages.

simulation.label: FICTIONAL LEARNING SCENARIO — NOT OPERATIONAL GUIDANCE
simulation.title: A coordination gap after a rapid-onset flood
simulation.setting: A fictional country, Rivarno. No real beneficiary data, sensitive locations or operational instructions are used. This scenario and all names in it are invented for training purposes only.
objectives: Practice weighing incomplete, conflicting information before acting.
Connect a coordination decision to humanitarian principles and inclusion of local actors.
See how an early choice changes what information becomes available next, without a single 'correct' path.
simulation.role_limits: You are role-playing a fictional Humanitarian Coordination Officer. This is a training exercise: it carries no real authority, and nothing in it is operational guidance for an actual response.

steps.prompt: Three days after a flood in fictional Rivarno, two cluster leads give you different severity estimates for the same district, and a local NGO network says it was not consulted on either. You must recommend how the next 48 hours of coordination meetings are run.

choices.text: Go with the higher severity estimate to be safe, and proceed to planning.
choices.consequence: Faster planning, but the unreconciled numbers resurface later, and the local network's exclusion is not addressed — a transparency and inclusion cost.

choices.text: Pause 24 hours to reconcile the two estimates and bring the local network into the next meeting.
choices.consequence: Slower start, but the next round of information is more reliable and more representative — at the cost of a day's delay in a fast-moving situation.

choices.text: Run both estimates in parallel without reconciling, and decide later.
choices.consequence: Avoids an immediate choice, but downstream plans end up built on two incompatible baselines, which surfaces as confusion in step 2.
